Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the share award scheme is funded from existing shares and no convertibles or options exist.

inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. fx_rate is HKD per CNY = 1.1724 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16; the inverse HKDCNY=X print of 0.8505 on 2026-10-17 implies 1.1758, a 0.3% spread). No dual listing exists for a parity check; direction check instead: the FY2025 final dividend was declared at HK$1.22 = RMB1.06 per share (interim note 8), i.e. 1.151 HKD/CNY in March 2026 -- the rate has since moved toward 1.17 as the RMB appreciated, which is the same move that produced the RMB475m FX loss on the HKD IPO proceeds in H1 FY2026. All per-share values are computed in CNY and converted at 1.1724; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are in HKD to match current_price.

inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8%, China equity risk premium ~7.0%, beta ~1.1 for a HK-listed Chinese consumer-durables manufacturer -> cost of equity ~9.5%. The company is net cash with RMB2.5bn of 0.6-3.65% bank loans, so WACC ~ cost of equity = 9.5%. No ad-hoc small-cap, governance or cyclicality premium is stacked on top: those risks are charged once, in the scenario flows and the 35% bear weight. Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Lease liabilities RMB91.0m (12.662 current + 78.379 non-current, 30 Jun 2026) are included in total_debt; lease principal (RMB8.7m in H1 FY2026) is NOT deducted from the flows; ROU depreciation stays inside D&A as a non-cash charge. Ongoing renewal of the leasehold-land ROU assets (RMB1,542m, mostly prepaid PRC land-use rights) is charged through the capex path, which folds in the 'Purchase of leasehold land' investing line (RMB410.7m FY2025, RMB105.1m FY2024) that the Metrics CSV keeps as the LeasingLandPurchases KPI rather than inside capex.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required: 100% of profit is attributable to owners of the parent (no non-controlling interests on the balance sheet).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year horizon -- an operating manufacturer (household and central air-conditioners, ~87%/11% of revenue) routed via the SKILL.md table row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file (currency, leases, matching asset, SBC-near-zero, charge risk once). Not a bank/REIT/holdco and no live corporate action. Treated as a cyclical: FY2024 (13.7% underlying EBITDA margin) was a subsidy-fuelled peak, FY2025 11.0%, H1 FY2026 11.9% (H2 seasonally ~8.5%), so the base case sits on a mid-cycle 11% rather than the peak. CASH: 'cash and bank balances' 7,736.6 plus bank wealth-management products held at FVTPL 1,260.0 current + 50.0 non-current = 9,046.6; these are the matching assets for the interest income (RMB164.6m FY2025, RMB110.7m H1 FY2026) and FV gains stripped from the flows. Pledged deposits of 3,397.7 (2,752.1 current + 645.6 non-current) are EXCLUDED from cash: they secure bills payable to suppliers and are operating working capital, and their movement is already inside OCF. DEBT: interest-bearing bank borrowings 1,875.0 current + 658.5 non-current = 2,533.5, plus lease liabilities 91.0. EQUITY BRIDGE: the FY2025 final dividend (HK$1.22/sh = RMB1,683.5m) was declared in H1 FY2026 but unpaid at 30 June (no dividends-paid line in H1 financing; it sits in other payables, which rose 4,437 -> 6,540); it has since been paid and a buyer today does not receive it, so it is deducted. EBITDA DEFINITION: the CSV ebitda = PBT + finance costs + D&A, which still contains interest income, FX and derivative marks; the margin anchors above strip all three (FY2025: 3,596.8 - 164.6 interest - 167.5 derivative gain + 27.7 FX loss = 3,292 = 11.0%; H1 FY2026: 1,744.8 - 110.7 interest - 4.2 FV gain + 474.9 FX loss + 23.1 derivative loss = 2,128 = 12.2%; FY2024: 4,155.3 - 217.8 - 16.4 + 165.1 = 4,086 = 13.7%). The RMB474.9m H1 FY2026 exchange loss is the translation of HKD/USD cash as the RMB appreciated and is excluded from the operating margin; its economic effect is already in the lower RMB cash balance. WORKING CAPITAL: the business runs structurally NEGATIVE net operating working capital (trade and bills payables 13,048 + contract liabilities 1,731 + other payables ex-dividend ~4,856 versus receivables 5,470 + FVOCI receivables 1,197 + inventories 5,157 + prepayments 1,422), i.e. suppliers and dealer prepayments fund the stock -- so growth releases cash and contraction consumes it; wc_capture is a small POSITIVE 5% in base (0% bear, 8% bull), applied to the revenue change, which makes the FY2026 revenue decline a cash cost. TAX: Ningbo AUX holds HNTE status at 15% to Dec 2027; other PRC subsidiaries 25%; FY2025 cash tax paid 655.6 = 22.7% of PBT, FY2024 20.0%, H1 FY2026 effective 19.6%; a 75% payout from PRC subsidiaries to the Cayman parent attracts 5-10% dividend withholding, so the path ramps 21% -> 25% by FY2029 as the HNTE concession is assumed to lapse and withholding leakage persists. SBC-NEAR-ZERO: SBC is 0.04% of revenue; house and street values coincide within rounding and band_position is not meaningful (reported as degenerate by the engine; read it as n/a). Buybacks: none ever; the flat share count is a modelling convention the company has not had to fund, but with SBC at RMB12m/yr the point is academic. CAPEX: FY2024 925 PP&E+intangibles (+105 land) = 3.5% of revenue; FY2025 1,409 (+411 land) = 6.1%; H1 FY2026 945 (annualising ~6.3%), funded by the ~HK$2.0bn (50%) of IPO proceeds earmarked for manufacturing/supply-chain -- the Wuhu compressor plant and overseas capacity -- so capex runs at 6% in FY2026 and glides to a 3% maintenance level by FY2030 while D&A rises from 2.16% (FY2025) to 2.7% on the larger asset base. REVENUE FY2026: H1 -12.9% to 17,504; H2 is seasonally ~1/3 of the year (H2 FY2025 9,964); base assumes H2 ~ -5% for a full-year ~27,000 (-10%); bear -14%, bull -7%. No company numeric guidance exists; the only external marker is a Huaxi Securities FY2026 net-profit estimate around RMB2.2bn, which the base case does NOT adopt (base FY2026 NOPAT ~1.6bn).
inputs.dividend_policy_note: Board commitment to a payout of not less than 75% of profit attributable to owners for each of FY2025-FY2027. At the base case this is ~RMB1.2-1.3bn/yr (HK$0.9-0.95/sh, a ~11-12% yield at the current price) and is broadly covered by owner FCF plus the RMB6.4bn net-cash pile; the DCF values the flows, not the distribution, so the commitment is a cross-check on cash availability rather than a value lever. H1 FY2026 interim dividend status was not checked and would be a further post-balance-sheet cash outflow.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: average of the base-case FY2027-FY2035 growth path (mid-cycle). Equity CAGR (79%) is distorted by the Sep-2025 IPO (RMB3.86bn capital reserve) and the RMB3.79bn pre-IPO FY2024 dividend; the 15.4% revenue CAGR runs FY2022 trough to the FY2025 subsidy-cycle peak and is not a forward rate (FY2025 revenue +1.0%, H1 FY2026 -12.9%).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR 79.2% vs revenue 15.4% / net income 15.7%: divergence >30%, caused by IPO proceeds and a pre-IPO special dividend rather than by operating compounding. Equity CAGR is unusable as a growth anchor for this ticker.
historical_growth.notes: History is three annual periods (FY2022-FY2023 are comparative-table rows from the FY2025 financial summary; FY2024-FY2025 full statements) plus three interims -- the company listed in September 2025 and no deeper history exists. Owner FCF: FY2024 1,592.9 reported - 4.2 SBC - 217.8 interest income = 1,370.8; FY2025 1,477.6 - 12.4 - 164.6 = 1,300.7 (-5.1%); H1 FY2026 147.1 - 5.7 - 110.7 = 30.7 vs H1 FY2025 1,206.8, on higher capex, a seasonal RMB2.45bn contract-liability unwind and a RMB770m increase in pledged deposits. Reported FCF excludes leasehold-land purchases (FY2025 410.7) which the forward capex path includes. SBC-adjusted and reported FCF series are within 1% of each other: SBC is not a growth-absorbing cost here.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue -10% (H1 -12.9% actual, H2 ~-5%), then a low-single-digit recovery as overseas sales companies (3-5 added per year) and central AC offset a flat-to-shrinking China household market. EBITDA margin holds at a mid-cycle 10.5-11.0% -- below the 13.7% FY2024 subsidy peak, above the ~8.5% seasonal H2 trough -- as central AC mix (31% GM) and in-house compressors offset price-war pressure in household (16% GM). Capex 6% of revenue in FY2026 while IPO proceeds are deployed, gliding to 3% maintenance by FY2030. Cash tax ramps 21% -> 25% as the HNTE 15% concession lapses after 2027 and dividend withholding on a 75% payout persists. Terminal: 12x owner FCF cap for a cyclical #5 player.

bull.narrative: Middle East demand and ODM orders normalise in H2 FY2026 (revenue -7%), then 5-7% growth for four years as Japan/Indonesia/Argentina entries and the AUFIT/ShinFlow premium brands add share. Central AC (data-centre cooling, heat pumps) grows to ~15% of revenue and the Wuhu compressor plant lifts household unit margins, taking EBITDA margin back to a 13% plateau -- roughly the FY2024 peak, held rather than exceeded. Growth-funded capex stays above 3% until FY2032. Terminal 14x cap and 2.5% growth: still a cyclical, but a re-rated one.

bear.narrative: H2 FY2026 is as weak as H1 (revenue -14%) and FY2027 falls another 3% as ODM customers (39% of revenue) keep de-stocking, US/EU tariffs bite and the RMB stays strong. Midea/Gree/Haier and Xiaomi hold a price war in the China replacement market; household GM slips toward 14%, EBITDA margin settles at 8.8% -- the H2 FY2025 seasonal trough becomes the annual run-rate. The Wuhu capex is sunk on a smaller revenue base (D&A 2.9%), the HNTE concession lapses and withholding leakage pushes cash tax to 26%. Dealer prepayments stop funding the business (wc capture 0). Terminal 10x cap, 1.5% growth. Revenue does not regain FY2025 levels within the horizon.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle normalisation. The axes that matter for AUX are (1) China household AC demand after the trade-in subsidy withdrawal, (2) ODM export order volatility and tariffs, (3) the RMB, which hits ~50% of revenue, (4) copper/aluminium input costs, and (5) whether central AC and premium sub-brands can shift mix fast enough to hold margin against a Midea/Gree/Haier price war. Base assumes none of these breaks decisively either way: FY2026 is a -10% revenue year with an 10.5% EBITDA margin, followed by 2-4% growth and an 11% mid-cycle margin, capex normalising to 3% once IPO-funded capacity is built, and the 75% payout funded from flows plus the RMB6.4bn net cash.
scenario_narratives.bull: Cyclical recovery plus mix shift. Middle East and ODM demand recover in 2027, overseas sales companies compound, central AC/data-centre cooling and AUFIT/ShinFlow lift blended margin to a 13% plateau (the FY2024 peak, not exceeded), and in-house compressors give a durable unit-cost edge. The market re-rates a 12% dividend yield, net-cash #5 player from ~2x EV/EBITDA toward a 14x FCF exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural squeeze. ODM keeps shrinking under tariffs and a strong RMB, China household stays in a price war led by scaled incumbents and Xiaomi, margins settle at the seasonal-trough 8.8%, and the IPO capex is sunk on a smaller base. Revenue never regains FY2025 levels in the horizon. Governance and controlling-shareholder (AUX Holdings conglomerate, 82% owner) risks are not modelled as a separate cash leakage but are the reason this scenario carries 35% weight rather than the 15% default.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 35/45/20. Bear up: thirteen months of listed history, a March-2026 profit warning followed by a -41% H1, a 39%-of-revenue ODM line that fell 25% in six months, a distant #5 position against incumbents holding ~70% share, and an 82% controlling shareholder whose private conglomerate (property, healthcare, finance) is the kind of related-party exposure the market is visibly discounting at a ~5x P/E. Bull down: the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once -- Middle East recovery, ODM re-ordering, RMB stabilising, copper easing, AND a mix shift to central AC -- so 20% rather than 35%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AUX is a cyclical, low-moat, net-cash manufacturer valued on mid-cycle owner FCF rather than on either the FY2024 subsidy peak or the H1 FY2026 trough. Interest income and WMP fair-value gains are stripped from the flows and the matching RMB9.0bn of cash and WMPs added back once; pledged deposits that secure bills payable are treated as operating and excluded; the declared-but-unpaid FY2025 dividend is deducted. The terminal is capped at 12x owner FCF in base (10x bear, 14x bull) because the market has never paid a compounder multiple for a #5 Chinese white-goods maker; any value above the no-re-rate ~2-3x EV/EBITDA the stock trades at today is a re-rating thesis, and the entry price at a 15% hurdle is the figure that does not depend on it. House and street bases coincide because SBC is 0.04% of revenue.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly RMB3bn of base equity value; the 11% mid-cycle assumption sits between a 13.7% peak and an 8.5% seasonal trough

Cash quality and governance: RMB9.0bn of cash/WMPs sits in PRC subsidiaries under an 82% controlling shareholder with a sprawling private group; the DCF takes it at face value, the market plainly does not
ODM/tariff/RMB: ~50% of revenue is export, 39% is third-party ODM; a 10% RMB move or a US tariff step changes FY revenue by high single digits with little offset
Dividend commitment vs capex: 75% payout plus 6% capex in FY2026 exceeds owner FCF in a weak year; sustained, it draws down the net cash the valuation adds back

Terminal cap: the 12x FCF cap binds in base, so the valuation is a function of the exit multiple assumption as much as of the growth rate; at the stock's current ~3x EV/FCF the implied exit multiple is a 4x re-rating

Tax: the HNTE 15% concession to Dec 2027 is assumed to lapse; renewal would add ~2pp to NOPAT, and dividend withholding on the Cayman structure could run higher than the 25% path if the payout is maintained
